Hi Sarah / Glen — thanks, good questions. Below is an indicative breakdown (high-level, non-binding) to help procurement. I’ll follow up with a one-pager and an Excel with per-token math.

1) Unit-economics by volume band (indicative net cost to customer for Private/VPC deployment):
- Pilot (50M tokens/mo): $1200 — $3000 per 1M tokens (high because fixed infra amortized across low volume)
- Initial (500M tokens/mo): $180 — $480 per 1M tokens
- Steady-state (2B tokens/mo+): $40 — $140 per 1M tokens

Notes: ranges depend on model size (base vs large), quantization, caching effectiveness, and whether you use autoscaling vs reserved capacity. We expect most fintech workloads to land in the lower half of the bands once optimized (strong KV/prefix caching + batching).

2) Licensing model (two common options we propose):
- Option A — Per-environment license + annual platform fee: fixed fee per named environment (prod/staging/dev), includes Private control plane + standard support. Good when you need clear isolation and predictable per-env pricing.
- Option B — Capacity/reserved (Dedicated-style) + private add-on: commit to a reserved GPU capacity (monthly/annual) that covers multiple environments; usually lower unit cost at scale but needs a commit.

Example for your stated environments (2 prod shards, 1 staging, 2 dev):
- Option A estimate: 5 environments -> 5 * environment fee + platform fee.
- Option B estimate: 1 reserved pool sized for peak steady-state throughput; staging/dev share burst capacity. We’d size the pool using expected steady-state RPS and concurrency.

3) Support tiers (indicative):
- Standard: Business-hours support, email response SLA (4 business hours), monitoring access — included with platform fee.
- Enterprise: 24/7 critical incident support, 1 named technical account manager, quarterly reviews — +15–25% on top of base license pricing.
- Platinum: Enterprise benefits + dedicated remote onboarding, custom playbooks, monthly on-call with assigned SRE — +30–50% (for strategic customers).

4) Environment licensing implications:
- Per-environment licenses treat each cluster as a billed unit; multiple prod shards count as multiple environments.
- Reserved-capacity pools can be shared across shards/environments (lower cost) but require traffic isolation controls if required by compliance.

Next steps: if you can confirm a target pilot band (50M vs 100M) and a steady-state target, we’ll produce an indicative quote showing both Option A and B with estimated annual costs and unit $/1M tokens. Also happy to include a sample SOW for procurement.

I’ll attach a short one-pager and the detailed spreadsheet in the next email.

Best,
Ben

Quick clarification on environment topology from our side — based on Ben’s notes and typical fintech setups, here’s how we’d map your items to "environments":
- Prod: 2 prod clusters (count as 2 environments for per-env licensing) — active/active for high availability
- Staging: 1 environment used for release testing and perf tuning

If FinTechCo is comfortable consolidating dev, that brings the environment total to 5 (2 prod + 1 staging + 2 dev). If not, and you want 2 separate dev clusters per team, update us and we’ll reflect 6+ envs in Option A pricing.
